description: §23.2.4a positive, executed — `await /'/.exec(s)` (and the same split across lines) is a SINGLE EXPRESSION whose operand is a regex literal: codegen injects the `return` and the value crosses (`v`, `w` = "'"). Whether `/` starts a regex depends on the grammar of the slice's real context (the body of an async function, where `await` is an operator); a standalone lexer reads `await` as an identifier, the `/` as division and the `'` as an unterminated string. Before the s456 review fix that misread made the slice a statement body with no `return`, settling silently to `not`.
rationale: §23.2.4a: a slice with no top-level `;` and no top-level `return` is a single expression and codegen injects the `return`; a slice is evaluated as the body of a strict-mode async function, so it is read in that context.
